name: V
appears: The whole game · all three prologues (Nomad, Streetkid and Corpo)
note:
Valerie or Vincent, depending on the body and voice you pick when you create the character. A Night City merc whose lifepath (Nomad, Streetkid or Corpo) only changes the prologue and some dialogue. After the Konpeki Plaza heist in The Heist, V is left with the **Relic** in their head: a biochip carrying Johnny Silverhand's engram that slowly erases V's mind. The rest of the story is the search for a way out. Romances depend on body and voice, not lifepath: **Judy** needs a feminine body and voice, **River** a feminine body, **Panam** a masculine body and **Kerry** a masculine body and voice. English voices: Cherami Leigh (feminine) and Gavin Drea (masculine).

**Spoiler:** in The Devil V signs Secure Your Soul on Arasaka's orbital station or returns to Earth with about six months to live; in The Star V leaves Night City with the Aldecaldos; in The Sun V becomes an Afterlife legend; in Temperance V crosses into cyberspace and Johnny keeps the body; in The Tower V spends two years in a coma, has the Relic removed and can no longer use combat cyberware. Path of Least Resistance is V's suicide.

name: Johnny Silverhand
role: Rockerboy and terrorist; the Relic's engram
appears: From Love Like Fire to the endings · Chippin' In and Blistering Love · Kerry's chain · Phantom Liberty
note:
Robert John Linder, former Samurai guitarist and U.S. Army veteran. In 2023 he bombed Arasaka Tower; Adam Smasher killed him that same day and his mind was trapped with Soulkiller. His engram lives in the Relic and shares V's head. You play him directly in Love Like Fire and on Rogue's route. Tapeworm tracks your affinity with him, but what unlocks Blistering Love and the secret ending are your answers at his grave in Chippin' In: the famous 70% affinity requirement is a myth. English voice: Keanu Reeves (singing: Dennis Lyxzén).

**Spoiler:** in The Devil his engram is removed from V; in The Star and The Sun V keeps the body and Johnny leaves with Alt beyond the Blackwall (exact wording unconfirmed); in Temperance he keeps V's body and leaves Night City by bus; in The Tower he dies when the Relic is removed.

name: Jackie Welles
appears: Prologues and Act 1 (The Rescue to The Heist) · Heroes · Nocturne Op55N1
note:
V's partner through all of Act 1: an ex-Valentino, Mama Welles' son and Misty's boyfriend. He and V take the Konpeki Plaza heist Dex offers them, the job that was meant to put them in the big leagues. Each lifepath introduces him differently, but all three prologues end with him. In Heroes you receive his **La Chingona Dorada** pistols and his **ARCH** bike. English voice: Jason Hightower.

**Spoiler:** he always dies at the end of The Heist; no choice prevents it. Then you choose where his body goes: send it home to Mama Welles and you get the full Heroes ofrenda; send it to Viktor and you get the short version, and you can talk to his engram on the rooftop before the final assault.

name: Dexter DeShawn
role: Fixer behind the Konpeki Plaza heist
appears: The Ride · The Pickup · The Information · The Heist · Playing for Time
note:
"Dex", a Night City fixer back after years off the grid. He hires V and Jackie to steal an Arasaka biochip at Konpeki Plaza, with T-Bug as netrunner, the Militech Flathead robot they get in The Pickup and Evelyn Parker as the client. In The Information, Evelyn offers V a way to cut him out. A Corpo V can ask him for a bigger cut in the prologue. His bodyguard is Oleg Darkevich. English voice: Michael-Leon Wooley.

**Spoiler:** when the heist goes wrong he shoots V in the head and dumps the body in the Municipal Landfill. Takemura kills him on the spot at the start of Playing for Time; he always dies.

name: T-Bug
role: Netrunner on V and Jackie's crew
appears: Practice Makes Perfect · The Rescue · The Information · The Heist
note:
A freelance netrunner from the Afterlife circle, sometimes just called "Bug". She is with you in the tutorial and backs V and Jackie up from the net in The Rescue and The Information. In The Heist she opens Konpeki Plaza's doors and cameras remotely. She can be toasted in Unfinished Sympathy (Phantom Liberty). English voice: Cynthia Kaye McWilliams.

**Spoiler:** she always dies in The Heist: when Yorinobu locks the hotel down she is flatlined in the middle of the escape.

name: Viktor Vektor
role: Ripperdoc in Little China (Watson) and V's mentor
appears: The Ripperdoc · The Heist · Playing for Time · Heroes · Nocturne Op55N1 · every ending
note:
"Vik", a former boxer and V's trusted ripperdoc. His clinic is in the alley off Urmland Street, behind Misty's Esoterica, in Little China (Watson). In The Ripperdoc he installs Basic Kiroshi Optics and a Ballistic Coprocessor (plus Subdermal Armor) for €$21,000, which you pay on the spot or owe him. After that he sells the standard stock, which refreshes every 10 levels. After The Heist he patches V up again in Playing for Time. English voice: Michael Gregory.

**Spoiler:** he is alive in every ending and leaves you a message in the credits of each one. In The Tower, Zetatech buys his clinic and he works for them while it is renovated.

name: Misty Olszewski
role: Owner of Misty's Esoterica; Jackie's girlfriend
appears: The Ripperdoc · The Heist · Playing for Time · Heroes · Nocturne Op55N1 · the endings
note:
She runs Misty's Esoterica, an esoteric shop on Urmland Street (Watson), right in front of Viktor's clinic. She reads tarot and gives V the bullet necklace. In Heroes you can reconcile her with Mama Welles. Before the final assault, in Nocturne Op55N1, she hosts the rooftop where you choose who goes with you to Arasaka Tower. English voice: Erica Lindbeck.

**Spoiler:** she survives every ending and calls in the credits with a different tarot reading for each, except The Tower. In The Devil, Viktor says she left for Warsaw; in The Tower, Zetatech has bought the shop, she helps V back on their feet and is moving to Poland.

name: Mama Welles
role: Jackie's mother; owner of El Coyote Cojo
appears: The Heist · Playing for Time · Heroes
note:
Guadalupe Alejandra Welles, Jackie's mother and owner of El Coyote Cojo, the Heywood bar where the Streetkid prologue begins. She gives you Heroes, the ofrenda for her son, with the family, Padre and the Valentinos. For the full ofrenda you must have sent Jackie's body home at the end of The Heist. At the ofrenda you can ask her to be kinder to Misty. English voice: Krizia Bajos.

**Spoiler:** she lives. She only calls in the credits if you finished Heroes: she prays for V in the endings where V dies, is amused by V's fame in The Sun and The Devil, and is horrified in The Star.

name: Evelyn Parker
role: Doll and client of the Konpeki heist
appears: The Ride · The Information · The Heist · Automatic Love · The Space in Between · Disasterpiece · Double Life
note:
A doll, formerly of Clouds, and Yorinobu Arasaka's ex-lover: she is the client of the Konpeki Plaza heist. In The Information she meets V at Lizzie's, the Mox club, introduces Judy and offers to cut Dex out. When the heist goes wrong she disappears, and finding her is Judy's thread in Act 2: Automatic Love takes you to Clouds and Woodman, and The Space in Between to the Scavenger den where you find her. Her leads also take you to the Voodoo Boys. English voice: Kari Wahlgren.

**Spoiler:** she always dies. After what Woodman did to her, she takes her own life at the start of Judy's chain; no earlier choice prevents it.

name: Judy Álvarez
appears: The Information · Automatic Love · The Space in Between · Disasterpiece · Double Life · Judy's chain · endings
note:
A braindance tech who works with the Mox at Lizzie's and lives in Kabuki. She teaches you braindance editing in The Information and searches for Evelyn with you in Act 2. Her chain runs from Both Sides, Now to Pyramid Song, and Pisces decides the fate of Clouds. **Romance** (feminine body and voice): accept her plan in Ex-Factor, side with her in Pisces without taking Maiko's bribe (up to €$37,200, which locks the romance), kiss her in Pyramid Song and don't leave while she sleeps. English voice: Carla Tassara.

**Spoiler:** in The Star she leaves Night City with V (Carol drives her to the camp); in The Sun she ends it and leaves; in The Devil she leaves the city; in Temperance she leaves a sorrowful voicemail; in The Tower she lives in Pittsburgh, married to Bianca, and the romance is over.

name: Goro Takemura
appears: Playing for Time · Down on the Street · Gimme Danger · Play It Safe · Search and Destroy · Nocturne Op55N1 · The Devil
note:
Saburo Arasaka's bodyguard, loyal to his late master's memory. He pulls V out of the landfill in Playing for Time and offers a deal: reach Hanako so Arasaka can fix the Relic. His Act 2 line runs through Down on the Street, Gimme Danger and the parade in Play It Safe. He resents V for killing Oda, if you do. Saving him in Search and Destroy is needed for The Devil achievement and for Oda to fight on your side in Totalimmortal. English voice: Rome Kanda.

**Spoiler:** he dies in Search and Destroy if you don't go back for him. Alive, he offers you Secure Your Soul in The Devil; in The Sun, The Star and Temperance he calls to tell you to rot in hell; in The Tower he is in hiding, accused of Hanako's murder after a failed coup.

name: Hanako Arasaka
role: Saburo's daughter; patron of The Devil ending
appears: Playing for Time · Down on the Street · Gimme Danger · Play It Safe · Search and Destroy · Nocturne Op55N1 · The Devil
note:
Saburo Arasaka's daughter, a self-taught netrunner and head of the corporation's Kiji faction. Takemura wants to reach her so she learns the truth about her father's death and helps V with the Relic. You kidnap her at the parade in Play It Safe, guarded by Oda, and her answer comes in Search and Destroy. On the Nocturne Op55N1 rooftop her offer is one of the options for the final assault. English voice: Alpha Takahashi.

**Spoiler:** in The Devil she lives and leads her father's restoration; if V turns the deal down, she calls in the credits offering six months working for Arasaka. In The Sun, The Star, Temperance and the secret ending she dies in Yorinobu's board purge (by his account); in The Tower she dies after the failed coup with Takemura.

name: Yorinobu Arasaka
role: Saburo's son and new head of Arasaka
appears: The Information · The Heist · Playing for Time · Nocturne Op55N1 · The Devil
note:
Saburo Arasaka's rebellious son, a former Steel Dragons member and an enemy of everything his family stands for. In The Heist, V and Jackie watch him kill his father at Konpeki Plaza, and he takes over Arasaka. He is the corporate antagonist of the main story, but you never fight him: the confrontation in Totalimmortal is dialogue only. English voice: Hideo Kimura.

**Spoiler:** in The Devil, Saburo's engram overwrites his body. In The Sun, The Star, Temperance and the secret ending he purges the board and sabotages Arasaka from within. In The Tower the board ousts him and he flees with nomads, according to the radio.

name: Saburo Arasaka
appears: The Heist · Love Like Fire · Play It Safe · The Devil
note:
"The Emperor": Arasaka's aged patriarch and CEO. In The Heist he arrives at Konpeki Plaza to meet his son, and Yorinobu kills him in front of V and Jackie, who are watching from hiding. In Johnny's 2023 memories in Love Like Fire, he is Johnny's interrogator. His death is the thread that drives Takemura and Hanako in Act 2, and his Iconic katana **Satori** is in his AV on the hotel roof. English voice: Masane Tsukayama.

**Spoiler:** he always dies in The Heist, but his engram is stored in Mikoshi. In The Devil it is loaded into Yorinobu's body.

name: Adam Smasher
role: Arasaka head of security; final boss
appears: The Heist · Love Like Fire · Play It Safe · Search and Destroy · the Arasaka Tower endings
note:
A full-body borg, Arasaka's head of security. In 2023 he killed Johnny at Arasaka Tower, and Johnny hates him for it. He shows up in the Love Like Fire memories, at Konpeki Plaza and at the parade, and he is the **final boss** of every ending that storms the tower: The Devil, The Star, The Sun and the secret ending. Since 2.1 he uses a Sandevistan and adapts to your playstyle, so boss guides from before that version no longer apply. He drops the Access Token you need to go on. English voice: Alec Newman.

**Spoiler:** he kills Saul in The Star and Rogue in The Sun. After beating him you decide whether to finish him or leave him (the consequence is unconfirmed). You don't meet him in The Tower.

name: Sandayu Oda
appears: Down on the Street · Play It Safe · Search and Destroy · The Devil
note:
Hanako Arasaka's personal bodyguard, a cyberninja with Mantis Blades and optical camo. You first see him in Down on the Street, and he is the **boss** of Play It Safe, when you kidnap Hanako during the parade. Beating him drops his Iconic katana **Jinchu-Maru**; if you miss it, Herold Lowe sells it in Phantom Liberty. Takemura resents V if you execute him. English voice: Noshir Dalal.

**Spoiler:** after the fight you kill him or spare him. If you spare him and Takemura is alive, he fights at your side for Hanako in Totalimmortal, in The Devil ending.

name: Anders Hellman
appears: Ghost Town · Lightning Breaks · Life During Wartime · Nocturne Op55N1 · The Devil
note:
The creator of Arasaka's Relic program, who spent a while at Kang Tao. Panam and V chase him through the Act 2 line from Ghost Town to Life During Wartime: you capture him at the Badlands gas station and question him at the Sunset Motel, where he talks about what the chip is doing to V. What you decide there changes whether he stays with Arasaka. If you have finished Phantom Liberty, you get new dialogue with him. English voice: Alec Newman.

**Spoiler:** he lives. In The Devil he escorts V to the Arasaka estate and, if Takemura died, he is the one who makes the final Secure Your Soul offer.

name: Panam Palmer
appears: Ghost Town · Lightning Breaks · Life During Wartime · Panam's chain · Nocturne Op55N1 · endings
note:
An ex-Aldecaldo turned merc, strong-willed and loyal to her people. She leads the Hellman line in Act 2 and, through her chain (Riders on the Storm to Queen of the Highway), unlocks The Star ending. **Romance** (masculine body, any voice): Saul must survive Riders on the Storm; side with her and touch her thigh; don't charge her for helping; in Queen of the Highway tell her the Basilisk is cozy. To be safe, help her kill Nash in Ghost Town: sources disagree on whether refusing locks the romance. English voice: Emily Woo Zeller.

**Spoiler:** in The Star she crosses the border with V; in The Sun it ends, but hopefully; in The Devil she leaves the city; in Temperance she vows to rip V out of Johnny's head; in The Tower she won't answer and Mitch asks you to stop calling.

name: Saul Bright
appears: Ghost Town · Panam's chain · Nocturne Op55N1 · The Star
note:
Head of the Aldecaldo clan, of the Bright family. In Riders on the Storm you have to rescue him, and if you take too long he can die and Panam's chain fails. In With a Little Help from My Friends you can tell him Panam's plan: he pays €$42,940, but it ends her chain. If the chain ends well, the Aldecaldos are the allies of The Star ending. English voice: Diarmaid Murtagh.

**Spoiler:** in The Star, Adam Smasher crushes him during Belly of the Beast. In the other endings, his credits message depends on how Panam's chain ended.

name: Mitch Anderson
appears: Ghost Town · Life During Wartime · Panam's chain · The Star · Temperance
note:
A Unification War veteran and friend of Panam and Scorpion. He pilots the **Basilisk**, the Aldecaldos' hover tank that you restore in Panam's chain and that carries everyone to Arasaka Tower in The Star. When Scorpion dies, Mitch sends him off in his car over a cliff, with V's help. English voice: Martin McDougall.

**Spoiler:** in The Star he survives badly wounded and crosses the border with the clan; his credits message changes with the ending. In The Tower he is the one who asks you to stop calling Panam.

name: Carol Emeka
appears: The Star · Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos
note:
One of the Aldecaldo clan's techies, of the Bright family, who also works as a netrunner. She is one of the allies of The Star ending: at the camp you can sit with her, Bob and Teddy at their table (stay until they finish talking or it doesn't count) and hear the plan with Cassidy, Mitch and Panam. In Phantom Liberty she is one of the netrunners you can call in Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos: she won't get you the data, but she sends a weapon or a quickhack for the fight (the exact requirements are unconfirmed). English voice: Fryda Wolff.

**Spoiler:** in The Star she survives and acts as a decoy in the sandstorm alongside Cassidy. If Judy is your partner, Carol is the one who drives her to the camp.

name: Scorpion
appears: Ghost Town · Life During Wartime · Panam's chain
note:
Driss Meriana, an Aldecaldo veteran and Mitch's old friend, who rides with Panam through the Act 2 Hellman line. You meet him with Mitch at the camp in Ghost Town, and he is back in action in Life During Wartime, at the site where the Kang Tao AV went down. When that job ends, Panam lets V keep his **Apollo** bike. Later he can be toasted at the With a Little Help from My Friends campfire and in Unfinished Sympathy. English voice: Noshir Dalal.

**Spoiler:** he always dies in Life During Wartime, defending the crashed AV. Mitch later sends him off in his Thorton Galena "Gecko", pushed over a cliff with V's help; the sources don't say which job holds that scene.

name: Bob Sagan
appears: The Star
note:
A techie of the Aldecaldo clan, of the Bright family, and a Unification War veteran like Mitch. He only matters in The Star ending: at the camp, before the assault, he sits with Carol and Teddy at a table to the west, and their talk only counts towards speaking with every nomad if you stay until they finish. Talking to him is dialogue only, with no rewards: what counts is the clan's send-off before they leave for Arasaka Tower in the Basilisk. English voice: Ako Mitchell.

**Spoiler:** he dies in the assault on Arasaka Tower in The Star, along with Teddy and Saul. If you come from that route and end in Temperance, the deaths are the same.

name: Nash
role: Leader of the gang that ambushed Panam
appears: The Heist (in passing) · Ghost Town · Panam's chain
note:
The leader of the gang that ambushed Panam's crew and took her truck. In The Heist you can see him arguing with Panam at the Afterlife. In Ghost Town, after you recover the truck in Rocky Ridge, you decide whether to help her kill him: agree and you get the **Widow Maker** (Herold Lowe sells it in Phantom Liberty if you miss it); refuse and you receive the **Archer Quartz "Bandit"**. Sources disagree on his gang: the wiki puts him with the Wraiths and the guide's job page talks of the Raffen Shiv. To protect a Panam romance, help her: they also disagree on whether refusing locks it.

**Spoiler:** if you help Panam, he dies in Ghost Town; if not, he dies when he turns up again in Queen of the Highway.

name: River Ward
appears: River's chain (I Fought the Law to Following the River) · the endings
note:
An NCPD detective. His chain starts with I Fought the Law, which Elizabeth Peralez gives you after Life During Wartime, and continues with The Hunt, the search for his nephew Randy, and Following the River, the family dinner. **Romance** (feminine body; the wiki contradicts itself on whether a feminine voice is also needed): pick **Edgewood Farm** in The Hunt, don't tell him to count you out, and choose romance at the water tower in Following the River. English voice: Robbie Daymond.

**Spoiler:** if you pick Poppy Farm, Randy dies, River blames you and ends up in jail. As a partner: in The Star he comes to the watchtower but stays in Night City and it ends; in The Sun and The Devil he waits for you and invites you to Randy's birthday; in Temperance he leaves a voicemail; in The Tower he sold NCPD intel to Trauma Team, is wanted and is too ashamed to see you.

name: Joss Kutcher
appears: The Hunt · Following the River
note:
River's sister, a single mother living in a trailer at the Red Peaks trailer park. Her son Randy is the kidnapped boy of The Hunt, and her trailer is one of the clue sites: in Randy's room, **Intelligence** helps you hack the computer and trace Harris's IP. If all goes well, in Following the River she welcomes you to the family dinner while River cooks jambalaya; with a feminine V, Joss makes it clear her brother likes you. English voice: Tonantzin Carmelo.

**Spoiler:** she lives. If you save Randy, she later texts you a photo of the family with him at the hospital.

name: Randy Kutcher
appears: The Hunt · Following the River
note:
Joss's son and River's nephew, missing before The Hunt begins. River recognizes him by the victim's shoes in a news clip about Peter Pan (Anthony Harris), and since Harris is in a coma, you go through his dreams as braindances to find where he is holding the boy. The farm you choose decides his fate, so **save before choosing**. Edgewood Farm has mines, four turrets and cameras; once you find him, don't leave the area or River and Randy die.

**Spoiler:** he survives if you pick **Edgewood Farm** and dies if you pick Poppy Farm. If River is your partner, he invites you to Randy's birthday in The Sun and The Devil; in The Tower, River paid for his treatment.

name: Anthony Harris
appears: The Hunt
note:
The serial killer the news calls "Peter Pan" and the public "Meatman", behind the kidnapping of River's nephew Randy. When The Hunt begins he is already in a coma, so River gets hold of his recorded dreams and you go through them as braindances to recognize the farm where he keeps his victims. Tracing his IP from Joss's trailer is one of the clues. Edgewood Farm, his hideout, has mines, turrets and cameras. If you have visited Edgewood Farm before, V recognizes the skyline when scanning the braindance.

**Spoiler:** his fate is unclear: the wiki lists him as alive in a coma, while the guide says that if you pick Poppy Farm, River kills him alone. It may depend on the branch.

name: Kerry Eurodyne
appears: Love Like Fire · Kerry's chain (Holdin' On to Boat Drinks) · the endings
note:
Samurai's former guitarist, now a solo rock star with MSM Records, living at Villa Eurodyne (North Oak). In Love Like Fire, Johnny can talk to him outside The Hammer. His chain opens through Johnny after Chippin' In and runs from Holdin' On to Boat Drinks: the Samurai reunion, the trouble with Us Cracks and his life offstage. **Romance** (masculine body and voice): get in his car in Rebel! Rebel!, because leaving him ends the chain; kiss him in Off the Leash and finish Boat Drinks. English voice: Matthew Yang King (singing: Damian Ukeje).

**Spoiler:** as a partner, in The Star he comes to the watchtower but stays and it ends; in The Sun and The Devil he waits for you; in Temperance he leaves a voicemail; in The Tower he is touring at the Crystal Palace and happy to pick up in a few months. If he is not your partner and made peace with Us Cracks, he goes on tour with them.

name: Denny
appears: Kerry's chain (Second Conflict)
note:
Samurai's former drummer, who lives in a mansion and used to be Henry's partner. She appears in Second Conflict, when Kerry wants to get the band back together for a gig: the gate is locked and nobody answers the intercom, so you let yourself in. In the garden, Henry has filled her pool with cement and they are arguing. You must pick who plays the gig; Johnny has no preference (he says Denny is a control freak and Henry can't be trusted). Pick Denny and Henry leaves angry. During the scene Denny throws a **gold-plated baseball bat** into the pool: loot it before you leave, because it is missable. English voice: Victoire Charles.

**Spoiler:** she lives; your choice only changes who plays and the final scene.

name: Henry
appears: Kerry's chain (Second Conflict)
note:
Samurai's former bassist, who spent a while at Blazetech and used to be Denny's partner. In Second Conflict, Kerry and V reach Denny's mansion and find Henry, who has filled her pool with cement from a truck. You must pick who plays the reunion gig; Johnny has no preference and reckons Henry can't be trusted. Pick Henry and Denny throws everyone out, and Kerry takes Henry to his car. Don't confuse him with Henry Sanchez, Steve's father in Temperance. English voice: Graham Vick.

**Spoiler:** he lives; your choice only changes who plays the gig and the final scene.

name: Steve Sanchez
role: West Wind kid who drives Johnny in Temperance
appears: Temperance
note:
A kid from the West Wind Apartments, in Pacifica, whom Johnny befriended; he dreams of being a musician and looks up to Kerry. He only appears in the Temperance ending, once Johnny has V's body: you call him on the intercom and ask for a ride. You can ask about the bruise (his dad, Henry Sanchez, hit him) and offer comfort or your alarm clock. His dad gets angry because Steve took the car keys, but always lets you go. He comes with you to Time Machine, where you try and buy a guitar for €$5000, and to the North Oak Columbarium. Don't confuse him with Steve Kowalski, a dead Wraith.

**Spoiler:** he lives; at the end, Johnny leaves him the guitar before boarding the bus.

name: Nancy Hartley
appears: Kerry's chain (Holdin' On · Second Conflict · A Like Supreme)
note:
Samurai's former keyboardist, now a Network News 54 journalist under the name **Bes Isis**. In Holdin' On, Johnny has to get her on board for the reunion, but her assistant Steven answers: she has been missing for two days after going to the Totentanz for a story. In Second Conflict you find her there according to what you did in The Pickup: if Royce lives, Dum Dum takes you to her peacefully; if Royce died, Patricia guides you and, if you didn't free Brick, you have to fight to get her out. Then you win her over in her car and she drops you at N54 News. English voice: Kosha Engler.

**Spoiler:** she lives and plays with Samurai at the A Like Supreme gig.

name: Blue Moon
appears: Kerry's chain (Rebel! Rebel! · I Don't Wanna Hear It)
note:
Aoi Tsuki, a member of **Us Cracks**, a J-pop group that wants to promote their tour with a cover of one of Kerry's songs. She is the friendliest of the three. In Rebel! Rebel! Kerry wants to blow up the van carrying the group's gear; in I Don't Wanna Hear It you find them at the Riot club in Little China, at 7 PM, and decide whether to hear them out or force them to drop the deal. Hear them out and they become friends with Kerry and you take the photo (with Cool, a selfie). A romance with her was discussed after launch, but it never made it into the game. English voice: Hiromi Dames.

**Spoiler:** her fate depends on the side job Every Breath You Take, which the guide doesn't cover.

name: Purple Force
appears: Kerry's chain (Rebel! Rebel! · I Don't Wanna Hear It)
note:
A member of **Us Cracks**, the J-pop group that wants to promote their tour with a cover of one of Kerry Eurodyne's songs. In Rebel! Rebel!, Kerry wants to blow up the van with their gear; you force the occupants out, take the access card and let them go. In I Don't Wanna Hear It you find all three at the Riot club in Little China, at 7 PM, and decide whether to hear them out or force them to drop the deal. Hear them out and they become friends with Kerry and you take the photo; with enough Cool, a selfie too. That agreement changes Kerry's credits message. English voice: Stephanie Sheh.

**Spoiler:** she lives.

name: Red Menace
appears: Kerry's chain (Rebel! Rebel! · I Don't Wanna Hear It)
note:
Akai Kyōi, the leader of **Us Cracks**, the J-pop group that wants to promote their tour with a cover of one of Kerry Eurodyne's songs. Kerry is not amused: in Rebel! Rebel! he wants to blow up the van carrying the group's gear. In I Don't Wanna Hear It, Kerry meets you at 7 PM at the Riot club in Little China, where they are, and there are several ways in. Inside you decide whether to hear them out or force them to drop the deal. Hear them out and they become friends with Kerry and you take the photo with the group; if he is not your partner and they reached an agreement, Kerry goes on tour with them in the credits.

**Spoiler:** her fate depends on jobs the guide doesn't cover.

name: Rogue Amendiares
role: Owner of the Afterlife; queen of the fixers
appears: Love Like Fire · Ghost Town · Transmission · Tapeworm · Chippin' In and Blistering Love · The Sun
note:
Night City's top fixer, owner of the Afterlife and Johnny's ex, who raided Arasaka Tower with him in 2023 (you live it in Love Like Fire). In Ghost Town she charges **€$15,000** for the Hellman lead, and in Transmission you convince her to help you with the Tower. Her chain is Chippin' In and Blistering Love, where she and Johnny meet again; it is not a romance for V. She is the ally of The Sun route. English voice: Jane Perry.

**Spoiler:** in The Sun, Smasher kills her in the tower's atrium. In the secret ending she survives and greets V at the Afterlife. In The Devil and The Star she lives and leaves a message for Johnny; in Temperance she is furious; in The Tower she welcomes V back, with Nibbles or the iguana beside her if you adopted them.

name: Alt Cunningham
role: Legendary netrunner, now an AI beyond the Blackwall
appears: Love Like Fire · I Walk the Line · Transmission · Never Fade Away · the Mikoshi endings
note:
Altiera Cunningham, the netrunner who created Soulkiller and Johnny's ex; she is now an AI beyond the Blackwall. In Love Like Fire, Johnny raids Arasaka Tower in 2023 to free her with a virus. In Transmission, the Voodoo Boys help you reach her on the net, and in Never Fade Away you relive her story with Johnny. She is not a romance for V: you only see her in Johnny's memories. English voice: Alix Wilton Regan.

**Spoiler:** she remains an AI in every ending. In The Star, The Sun, Temperance and the secret ending she takes control of Mikoshi; in The Sun she takes Johnny (or V) beyond the Blackwall. She plays no part in The Devil or The Tower.

name: Spider Murphy
appears: Love Like Fire
note:
Arabella "Spider" Murphy, the netrunner who joins Johnny, Rogue and Shaitan in the raid on Arasaka Tower on August 20, 2023. She only appears in Love Like Fire, the interlude where V relives Johnny's memories: they reach the tower by helicopter, you follow her through the floors and wait for her virus to upload into the network (it's called Liberator, per IGN) while Johnny plants the bomb. It is a linear job with no rewards and no level. English voice: Erica Lindbeck, who also voices Misty.

**Spoiler:** per the wiki she is alive as of 2023; the game doesn't say what became of her later.

name: Shaitan
appears: Love Like Fire
note:
The solo (combat merc) of Johnny's crew in the 2023 raid on Arasaka Tower, alongside Rogue and Spider Murphy. He only appears in Love Like Fire: he boards the helicopter with them outside The Hammer and fires the helicopter's gun as they attack the rooftop turrets. When he is hit, Johnny takes over the gun and keeps shooting. From there the rest of the raid is Johnny, Rogue and Spider. It is a linear job with no rewards and no level. English voice: Shai Matheson.

**Spoiler:** per the wiki he survives and is still alive in 2045; he never shows up in the game's present.

name: Jeremiah Grayson
appears: Chippin' In
note:
An Arasaka-linked ex-soldier who holds the leads Johnny is after in Chippin' In: his **Malorian Arms 3516** pistol and the whereabouts of his Porsche. You find him at the end of the ship at the Ebunike Docks, Maelstrom turf, after fighting the gang; the wiki ties him to the Wraiths. The fight ends with him **defeated, not dead**: you interrogate him (Smasher is in Japan), take back Johnny's gun and decide what to do with him. He hands over the access key to the **Porsche 911 Turbo (930)** container if you spare him, or you loot it from his body if you kill him; careful, killing him moves you off the ship at once and it's easy to forget the car. English voice: Stephen Oyoung.

**Spoiler:** if you kill him he gets a columbarium plaque. If you spare him, Ruby Collins, the dancer who gave you the lead, is killed later.

name: Crispin Weyland
appears: Chippin' In · The Sun · Temperance
note:
Known as "Squama", Rogue's bodyguard and one of the Afterlife mercs. In Chippin' In you talk to Weyland at the Afterlife before heading out after Johnny's car. The big role comes on The Sun route: in For Whom the Bell Tolls the objective is to follow Weyland through the Afterlife, and in Knockin' on Heaven's Door Weyland storms Arasaka Tower with Rogue and Johnny. When Smasher kills Rogue, Weyland fights him alongside Johnny. English voice: Mark Ebulué.

**Spoiler:** in The Sun, Weyland can die fighting Arasaka's troops or reach Mikoshi alive, depending on how the assault goes; if you end in Temperance from that route, the deaths are the same.

name: Placide
appears: M'ap Tann Pèlen · I Walk the Line · Transmission · The Damned
note:
The Voodoo Boys' enforcer and V's contact for reaching Alt. You meet him in M'ap Tann Pèlen, where he leaves his **Butcher's Cleaver** behind after killing the chicken (Herold Lowe sells it if you miss it). In I Walk the Line he gives you the job at Batty's Hotel (Coastview, Pacifica) and stays in touch while you go into the Grand Imperial Mall; he also plants malware on you. The choice about the NetWatch agent, Bryce Mosley, shapes everything that follows. In The Damned (Phantom Liberty), if you spared Placide and Brigitte, you can talk your way into Slider's hideout. English voice: Lovensky Jean-Baptiste.

**Spoiler:** if you took Mosley's deal, you fight him to get out of the church in Transmission and kill or spare him. Otherwise he survives, unless you choose to settle the score at the end.

name: Brigitte
appears: Double Life · M'ap Tann Pèlen · I Walk the Line · Transmission
note:
Maman Brigitte, leader of the Voodoo Boys and a netrunner set on crossing the Blackwall. She is the mysterious netrunner Evelyn talks to in the Double Life recording: the one who hired her to record the braindance of Yorinobu's penthouse. Mr. Hands gets V an audience with her in M'ap Tann Pèlen, and after I Walk the Line she receives you at Batty's Hotel. In Transmission she connects you with Alt through Johnny's engram. In The Damned, having spared her and Placide lets you talk your way in.

**Spoiler:** if you took Mosley's deal, Alt takes the Voodoo Boys for NetWatch and kills Brigitte and everyone connected. Otherwise her netrunners cross the Blackwall with Alt's help and she survives; at the end you can leave peacefully or settle the score.

name: Bryce Mosley
appears: I Walk the Line · Transmission
note:
The NetWatch agent attacking the Voodoo Boys' network from the Grand Imperial Mall, guarded by the Animals. You find him in the cinema's projection room at the end of I Walk the Line, and he tells you the Voodoo Boys plan to double-cross you. **Save before talking to him**: the choice is final. Take his deal and the shard and he removes Placide's malware but installs a NetWatch tracker. Knock him out and stay with the Voodoo Boys, and Placide's virus wipes out NetWatch facilities and nearly kills you too (the Relic saves you). While you fight, he tries to fry your brain with hacks. English voice: Shane Taylor.

**Spoiler:** he dies if you follow Placide's plan and survives if you take his deal; in that case, in Transmission Alt kills Brigitte and you fight Placide.

name: Nix
appears: Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos
note:
Rogue's netrunner at the Afterlife, formerly with Arasaka. He also sells quickhacks and crafting specs in Little China. He has his own side jobs, KOLD MIRAGE and Spellbound, outside the jobs the guide covers. In Phantom Liberty he is one of the netrunner options in Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos: if you finished KOLD MIRAGE and Spellbound and he is alive, he delivers the data **after 6 hours** at the Arasaka Memorial and gives you the **Self-ICE** implant, which blocks an enemy quickhack and is very handy against the MaxTac netrunner. English voice: Ako Mitchell.

**Spoiler:** he lives unless he dies in his own side jobs; that depends on your choices there.

name: Delamain
appears: The Heist · Playing for Time · Delamain chain · The Sun · Who Wants to Live Forever
note:
The AI that runs the Delamain cab company. He gets V out of Konpeki Plaza at the end of The Heist, and his core is at the HQ in Vista del Rey, Heywood. His job chain is about recovering his "divergent" cabs, which have slipped out of his control. When it ends, you decide what to do with the core. Update 2.5 fixed the cab that got stuck in Things Done Changed. English voice: Samuel Barnett (the divergents: Ellen McLain and Zach Villa).

**Spoiler:** at the end of his chain you can reset him (he loses his memories), merge him with the divergents (he evolves and leaves) or destroy the core (a successor AI takes over). In The Sun he pilots the AV if you didn't reset him; in The Tower he drives V to Viktor.

name: Meredith Stout
appears: The Ride · The Pickup
note:
A Militech agent (internal affairs per the guide; senior operations manager per the wiki) hunting the Flathead Maelstrom stole. In The Pickup you can call her before going to All Foods: she runs a lie-detector interrogation on you and offers a credchip to pay Royce with… and it carries a virus. A Corpo V can tell her they know about the virus. She has a **romantic encounter** (any body and voice): meet her without insulting her, take the chip and end things with Maelstrom violently after meeting Dum Dum, without the Body takedown on Royce, and reply nicely to her Act 2 message to unlock Venus in Furs.

**Spoiler:** if you follow her plan, she has Gilchrist killed and survives. If you refuse her chip or warn Royce, Gilchrist has her killed: her body turns up off a pier in north Watson.

name: Anthony Gilchrist
appears: The Pickup
note:
The Militech mole behind the Flathead theft: he leaked the convoy to Maelstrom. Meredith Stout suspects him and he is present at the lie-detector interrogation in the storm channel. On the outcomes where you don't follow Meredith's plan, he waits at the All Foods gate at the end of The Pickup and tells you you're even. A **Nomad** V can earn a crate of Militech gear: in a red-lit side room of the first big hall there is a computer with the message "Transports - LOA", from Gilchrist to Maelstrom; bring it up at the gate and the crate waits in your apartment. English voice: Akie Kotabe.

**Spoiler:** if you follow Meredith's plan, she has him killed. If not, he survives and he is the one who has Meredith killed.

name: Royce
appears: The Ride · The Pickup
note:
Simon Randall, Maelstrom's leader, who holds the Militech Flathead at the All Foods factory (Northside, Watson). In The Pickup you can pay him with the Militech chip, with your own money, or fight, and each outcome changes who walks out alive. The **peaceful deal** (don't meet Meredith, threaten nobody, get Jackie to sit and pay **€$10,000** of your own) is the only way to unlock the Maelstrom weapon vendor and keeps Dum Dum alive. If he fights, he is the job's **boss**, inside a Centaur exoskeleton. What happens to him decides how you get into the Totentanz in Second Conflict, in Kerry's chain.

**Spoiler:** he dies at V's hand (through dialogue or in the exosuit fight), at Militech's off-screen if you sneak out, or survives with the peaceful deal.

name: Dum Dum
appears: The Pickup · Kerry's chain (Second Conflict)
note:
Royce's spokesman in Maelstrom, who answers the All Foods intercom in The Pickup and leads you through the factory. A Streetkid V recognizes the **Black Lace** he offers and, if you leave on good terms with Maelstrom, Dum Dum gives you an extra one. If Royce survives, he returns in Second Conflict: he takes you through the Totentanz to Nancy without a fight and can drop his Iconic revolver **Doom Doom**; siding with Militech in The Pickup prevents it. If you miss it, Herold Lowe sells it in Phantom Liberty. Doom Doom can't be combined with getting Royce's Iconic Chaos.

**Spoiler:** he lives or dies depending on The Pickup; if he dies, he gets a columbarium niche.

name: Brick
role: Former Maelstrom leader, held at All Foods
appears: The Pickup · Kerry's chain (Second Conflict)
note:
Declan Griffin, Maelstrom's former leader, whom Royce keeps locked in a cell at All Foods. You can only find him on two of The Pickup's outcomes, and freeing him only pays off if Royce dies. His cell code is **9691**. If you free him and Royce dies, in Second Conflict (Kerry's chain) Patricia takes you to Nancy, who is meeting Brick, and there is no fight.

**Spoiler:** you free him, kill him or leave him in his cell. If you free him and Royce dies, he takes Maelstrom back.

name: Patricia Gerville
appears: The Pickup · Kerry's chain (Second Conflict)
note:
A gang member who shows up on Maelstrom turf after The Pickup. The wiki, on a very short page with no image, places her with 6th Street, although in Kerry's chain she is the one who guides you through the Totentanz, Maelstrom's club. Her role depends on what happened at All Foods: if Royce died, Patricia takes Dum Dum's place in Second Conflict. If you also freed Brick, she takes you straight to Nancy, who is meeting him; if you didn't, Nancy is locked up by the gang and you have to fight to get her out. If Royce is alive, you don't see her.

**Spoiler:** her fate depends on your choices and the guide doesn't detail it.

name: Sasquatch
role: Animals leader; I Walk the Line boss
appears: I Walk the Line
note:
Matilda K. Rose, leader of the Animals pack guarding the NetWatch agent at the Grand Imperial Mall. She is the **boss** of I Walk the Line: she stands guard at the cinema entrance with her hammer. If nobody detects you in the whole mall, the cinema gates stay open and **you can avoid her**. If you fight, bring thermal damage (her weakness) and quickhacks like Short Circuit and Overheat. She has a €$15,000 bounty per the wiki (game8 says 16k). Her **Sasquatch's Hammer** is missable. English voice: Krizia Bajos.

**Spoiler:** after the fight you kill or spare her. If you take Mosley's deal and spared her, the Animals let you leave in peace; if you follow Placide's plan, they attack you on the way out regardless.

name: Woodman
appears: Automatic Love · Ex-Factor
note:
Oswald Forrest, the dolls' "caretaker" at Clouds, the club on the 12th floor of Megabuilding H8 in Tyger Claws territory. In Automatic Love you question him in his office about Evelyn: he admits he sold her to the ripperdoc Fingers when he couldn't help her. High Intelligence, the Corpo lifepath, or having done Gig: Monster Hunt first (the Jotaro Shobo business) help him talk without a fight; if he turns hostile, the same lead is on his computer. **Save before entering his office**: Clouds takes your weapons. English voice: Joe Corrigall.

**Spoiler:** you kill him or leave him alive in Automatic Love. If he lives, Judy and V take revenge on him in Ex-Factor; if you killed him, that branch doesn't exist and Maiko is more hostile.

name: Fingers
appears: Automatic Love (lead) · The Space in Between · Disasterpiece · Judy's chain
note:
Finn "Fingers" Gerstatt, ripperdoc at Fingers M.D., on Jig-Jig Street in Japantown (Westbrook). Woodman left Evelyn with him as payment and he sold her to the Scavengers. In The Space in Between you go into his clinic with Judy and decide whether to punch him; his Iconic **Cottonmouth** is in his office or bedroom and is missable. As a vendor he has the standard ripperdoc stock: he sells from the start of Act 2 until The Space in Between, and again after Disasterpiece if you didn't punch him. English voice: Alex Ivanovici.

**Spoiler:** you can kill him later, optionally; if you do, you lose his shop for good.

name: Jotaro Shobo
appears: Gig: Monster Hunt · Automatic Love
note:
A Tyger Claw known as the "Devil of Kabuki", who makes and deals XBDs (illegal braindances). He is the target of Regina Jones' gig **Monster Hunt**, in Watson, which isn't one of the guide's jobs but is worth doing before Automatic Love: if you mention what happened to Jotaro, Woodman gives up the information about Evelyn on the spot, without a fight. Together with high Intelligence and the Corpo lifepath, it is one of the three ways to avoid combat at Clouds, where you go in unarmed. English voice: Yoshi Ando.

**Spoiler:** in Monster Hunt you kill him or abduct him to hand him over.

name: Sandra Dorsett
role: Night Corp netrunner rescued in The Rescue
appears: The Rescue · Down on the Street · Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos
note:
The Night Corp netrunner V and Jackie rescue from the Scavengers in The Rescue, the first Act 1 job. She survives if you get there in time and Viktor or Trauma Team take her. If Wakako still hasn't paid you for that job, in Down on the Street you can remind her of the Sandra Dorsett gig and collect what you're owed. In Phantom Liberty she is one of the netrunner options in Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos: if you resolved the job Full Disclosure in her favor, she delivers the data **after 8 hours** at Reconciliation Park and in return asks you to install a trojan in MaxTac. The wiki doesn't list her English voice.

**Spoiler:** she lives if you rescued her in time.

name: Maiko Maeda
appears: Automatic Love · Judy's chain (Ex-Factor · Pisces) · You Know My Name
note:
Judy's ex and one of the managers of Clouds, under Tyger Claws control. Judy recruits her for the plan to take the club from the Claws in Ex-Factor. In Pisces, Maiko **betrays the plan** in front of the bosses Hiromi Sato, Jun Azegami and Marcus Ichida and offers you money: €$27,900, or **€$37,200** with the Streetkid haggle. Taking it locks Pyramid Song and the Judy romance. **Save before Pisces.** Depending on your choices, she can show up at the Black Sapphire party in You Know My Name. English voice: Arina Ii.

**Spoiler:** in Pisces she becomes the owner of Clouds (if you take the bribe), dies, or is left alive while the dolls run Clouds, the kindest outcome.

name: Tom Caldera
appears: Automatic Love · Judy's chain
note:
A doll from the Clouds VIP area who helps V follow Evelyn's trail. In Automatic Love you enter his booth: he tells you Evelyn had an accident there and was sent to a "special clinic in Oslo", and sends you to Woodman. Later he joins Judy's revolt: in Talkin' 'bout a Revolution he shares the pizza with Judy, Roxanne and Maiko while they plan to take over the club. Don't confuse him with Tom of Tom's Diner. English voice: Shai Matheson.

**Spoiler:** in Pisces, the Tyger Claws kill him in retaliation whether you kill Maiko or leave her alive.

name: Roxanne Sumner
appears: Judy's chain (Talkin' 'bout a Revolution · Pisces)
note:
One of the Clouds dolls who join Judy's plan to take the club from the Tyger Claws. In Talkin' 'bout a Revolution she shares the pizza with Judy, Tom and Maiko while they organize the revolt, and in Pisces her fate depends on how the takeover ends. Don't confuse her with Roxanne Colton, "Roxxi", a 2020 merc who has nothing to do with Clouds. Judy's plan starts in Ex-Factor, when you agree to help her, and is settled by the Maiko choice at the end of Pisces. English voice: Alana Maria.

**Spoiler:** per the wiki she survives. If you kill Maiko, the Tyger Claws retake Clouds and Roxanne goes into hiding; if you leave Maiko alive and the dolls run the club, she still flees after the retaliation against Tom.

name: Hiromi Sato
role: Tyger Claw in charge of Clouds
appears: Judy's chain (Pisces)
note:
One of the Tyger Claws bosses who control Clouds and the target of Judy's plan in Pisces. The takeover runs through the maintenance level, the rooftop and Hiromi's balcony, where the **Tsumetogi** katana is. That is where the key moment comes: Maiko betrays the plan in front of Hiromi Sato, Jun Azegami and Marcus Ichida and offers you money to switch sides. Bring weapons to clear the Tyger Claws on the maintenance level and **save before Pisces**, because the Maiko choice decides the Judy romance. The wiki has only a short page on him, with no image or voice.

**Spoiler:** he dies in Pisces, either in the fight or at the hands of his own bosses with the Tsumetogi.

name: Claire Russell
appears: The Heist · The Sun
note:
The Afterlife's bartender, a former Militech employee and a street racer. In The Heist, while Dex is busy, you sit with Jackie at the bar and can talk to her. She has her own racing chain, which the guide doesn't cover as a job. After Jackie's death she puts his drink on the Afterlife menu, a detail worth looking for if you go back to the bar. On Rogue's route, before the assault, she offers you a special drink for the operation. English voice: Maddie Taylor.

**Spoiler:** she lives and, in The Sun's Path of Glory epilogue, serves you a special drink.

name: Lizzy Wizzy
appears: Side job Violence · You Know My Name
note:
Elisabeth Wissenfurth, a pop star whose body is almost all chrome. In the base game she appears in the side job **Violence**, at a motel, where she asks you to dispose of Liam's body. In Phantom Liberty she performs at the Black Sapphire party in You Know My Name: if you met her in Violence and didn't refuse to help, she recognizes you, and if you **compliment her performance** she gives you her **Amikiri Sound Cutter**; if you refused, she ignores you. Afterwards Alex sends a bootleg braindance of her show to your apartment. English voice: Grimes.

**Spoiler:** she lives in every case.

name: Jefferson Peralez
appears: The Peralez chain (Dream On) · the endings
note:
A Federalist Party candidate for mayor of Night City, the target of a conspiracy to control him. His wife Elizabeth gives you I Fought the Law after Life During Wartime, and their branch continues with Dream On: you investigate their apartment and the rooftop, chase a van and discover he is being manipulated. At the end you decide whether to tell him the truth: if you do, he plays along with his manipulators while trying to expose them; if you lie and blame Holt, he focuses on winning. English voice: Joseph May.

**Spoiler:** he wins the election in every ending. Your choice changes his credits call: paranoid about his wife if you told him the truth, or asking you for a job if you hid it.

name: Elizabeth Peralez
appears: I Fought the Law · Dream On
note:
Jefferson Peralez's wife and campaign organizer. She gives you I Fought the Law after Life During Wartime, and two branches grow from that job: River's (The Hunt and Following the River) and the Peralezes' (Dream On), which you can do in any order. In Dream On you talk to her before the final conversation with Jefferson, after the van chase. English voice: Kosha Engler.

**Spoiler:** she lives; how their marriage ends up depends on Dream On. If you tell Jefferson the truth, in the credits he is paranoid about her.

name: Mr. Blue Eyes
appears: Dream On · The Killing Moon · The Sun · secret ending
note:
A blue-eyed man with no known past, the power behind the conspiracy around Jefferson Peralez. Not even Viktor can find anything on him. In Phantom Liberty he is seen twice in The Killing Moon, on Songbird's path. His clearest role comes at the end: in the Path of Glory epilogue of The Sun (and of the secret ending) he is the one who offers you the Crystal Palace job. If you follow the Peralez plot, Dream On is where you first see the conspiracy he moves. English voice: Martin McDougall.

**Spoiler:** he is alive in every ending and his identity stays hidden.

name: Lucius Rhyne
appears: Only mentioned (Dream On backstory)
note:
Night City's mayor before the story begins. He was murdered with a virus-spiked braindance at the Red Queen's Race, a braindance club in Charter Hill, and acting mayor Weldon Holt covered up his death. He doesn't appear in any of the guide's jobs: he is the backstory of the Peralez chain. In I Fought the Law you visit the Red Queen's Race, where the boss's computer reveals Holt and Han, and you can interact with the braindance wreath in the booth. English voice: Paul Jerome.

**Spoiler:** he is already dead before the game begins.

name: Kirk Sawyer
role: Small-time fixer in the Streetkid prologue
appears: Streetkid prologue
note:
A small-time fixer threatening to break Pepe Najarro's legs over a debt. He only appears in the Streetkid prologue. You find him on the second floor of El Coyote Cojo, with **Big Joe**: he won't forgive the debt, but he offers a deal. Steal a **Rayfield Aerondight** belonging to an Arasaka corpo at Embers and he forgets what Pepe owes and gives you a cut. He hands you a device, a Rayfield service key, to open the car without tripping the alarm. At the end, Jackie tells you Kirk isn't as dangerous as he seems. English voice: Derek Hagen.

**Spoiler:** his fate depends on events outside the guide's jobs.

name: Pepe Najarro
appears: Streetkid prologue · Heroes
note:
The bartender at El Coyote Cojo, Mama Welles' bar in The Glen (Heywood). He opens the Streetkid prologue: V is at the bar setting their broken nose and Pepe tells them his trouble. He owes money to Kirk Sawyer, who is threatening to break his legs, and asks you to talk Kirk into forgetting the debt or settling it some other way. What you tell him only changes the conversation. He shows up again in Heroes: after the ceremony you can talk to him, as with Viktor, Padre and the Valentinos. English voice: Ronan Summers.

**Spoiler:** he lives.

name: Arthur Jenkins
appears: Corpo prologue
note:
V's boss in Arasaka's counterintelligence division, and he only appears in the Corpo prologue. He calls V, furious about a data leak in Frankfurt, and summons them to his office in Arasaka Tower. There he launches a cyberattack on the European Space Agency council to delay its vote on Arasaka's lunar licenses, and orders V to take out his superior and rival, Susan Abernathy, through their underworld contacts. He gives you a datashard with her details and cash (€$45,800, per IGN). English voice: Alec Newman.

**Spoiler:** the plan goes wrong and Arasaka fires V; the wiki lists Jenkins as deceased.

name: Susan Abernathy
appears: Corpo prologue
note:
Arasaka's Director of Special Operations, Arthur Jenkins' superior and rival. She only appears in the Corpo prologue: during Jenkins' cyberattack on the European Space Agency council, she calls to berate him. Jenkins orders V to kill her, but she already knows about the hit: at Lizzie's Bar, Arasaka agents demand the datashard with her details, strip V of their corporate privileges and disable their cyberware. That firing is what throws V onto the street and into working with Jackie. The wiki doesn't list her English voice.

**Spoiler:** the wiki lists her as deceased; the game doesn't show how.

name: Oleg Darkevich
appears: The Heist
note:
Dexter DeShawn's bodyguard. He appears at the Afterlife at the start of The Heist: after the bouncer lets you through and you sit with Jackie, you follow Oleg to Dex's booth, where Dex and T-Bug are waiting to go over the Konpeki Plaza plan. It is a short appearance, with no important dialogue or choices, but he is the face at Dex's side in the club. The wiki doesn't list his English voice.

**Spoiler:** the wiki doesn't say what became of him after Dex's death.

name: Wakako Okada
appears: The Rescue · Disasterpiece · Down on the Street · Playing for Time
note:
Westbrook's fixer, working from Jig-Jig Street in Japantown and dealing with the Tyger Claws (she once worked at Kiroshi). She pays for The Rescue: €$3,380. If she still hasn't paid, in Down on the Street remind her of the Sandra Dorsett gig and you collect; on that same visit she hands over the parade's security details. She also gives you a lead on the Disasterpiece XBD and a Tyger Claws tattoo that Cassius Ryder applies. Her gig Wakako's Favorite is where Chang-Hoon Nam, a Phantom Liberty netrunner, comes from. English voice: Ren Hanami.

**Spoiler:** she lives in every ending.

name: Regina Jones
appears: The Ripperdoc · The Ride · Watson gigs
note:
Watson's fixer, a former WNS journalist. She calls you in The Ripperdoc as V leaves the Megabuilding H10 apartment, and from then on she hands out Watson's gigs and the **Cyberpsycho Sightings**. One of her gigs, **Monster Hunt** (Jotaro Shobo), makes the talk with Woodman in Automatic Love easier. In Last Call, one of her jobs, the reward is the Iconic implant **Axolotl** (at Tier 5 if V is level 33 or higher). English voice: Alana Maria.

**Spoiler:** she lives in every ending.

name: Padre
appears: Streetkid prologue · Heroes
note:
Sebastian Ibarra, a former priest and ex-Valentino, Heywood's fixer. In the Streetkid prologue he waits outside El Coyote Cojo and drives you to Embers; on the way there is a brief run-in with Sam Carter, of 6th Street, and when you part he gives you his card. After that he hands out Heywood's gigs. In Heroes he is at Jackie's ofrenda and you can talk to him after the ceremony. English voice: Al Rodrigo.

**Spoiler:** he lives in every ending.

name: Dino Dinovic
appears: City Center gigs (outside the guide's jobs)
note:
City Center's fixer, who works out of the Electric Orgasm bar. He hands out City Center's gigs, which the guide doesn't cover as jobs. None of the guide's jobs puts him front and center, but he has a link to Phantom Liberty: Solomon Reed worked for him for a while as a bouncer while living undercover in Night City. English voice: Alec Newman, who per the wiki also voices Adam Smasher, Hellman, Jenkins and El Capitán.

**Spoiler:** he lives in every ending.

name: El Capitán
appears: Santo Domingo gigs (outside the guide's jobs)
note:
Muamar "El Capitán" Reyes, Santo Domingo's fixer. He hands out the gigs and jobs of Arroyo and Rancho Coronado, and none of the guide's jobs puts him front and center. Don't confuse him with Capitán Caliente, the restaurant that shows up in Lucretia My Reflection and Rebel! Rebel!: that's just a venue, not him. His gigs are optional work, paid in eddies and Street Cred. English voice: Alec Newman, per the wiki the same actor as Adam Smasher, Hellman, Jenkins and Dino Dinovic.

**Spoiler:** he lives in every ending.

name: Dakota Smith
appears: Badlands gigs · The Star
note:
The Badlands' fixer, known as "Mad Coyote", with her garage in Rocky Ridge and dealings with the Aldecaldos and the Pomo tribe. She hands out the Badlands gigs, which the guide doesn't cover as jobs. Her story appearance is in The Star ending: at the Aldecaldo camp, before leaving for Arasaka Tower, she is in the center of camp handing out **free weapons**. Talk to her before following Panam so you don't leave empty-handed. English voice: Sabra May.

**Spoiler:** she lives and gears you up at the camp in The Star ending.

name: Mr. Hands
appears: M'ap Tann Pèlen · most of Phantom Liberty
note:
Wade Bleecker, Pacifica's fixer, formerly with Petrochem. In M'ap Tann Pèlen he is the go-between with the Voodoo Boys and volunteers you for their job. In Phantom Liberty he is Dogtown's great broker: he feeds you information and work throughout the expansion, and in Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos his netrunner Yoko Tsuru (for €$15,000) is the route to the MaxTac Mantis Blades. After Firestarter his Tier 4 gigs open up. English voice: Alex Jordan since 2.0 (before that, Sean Power).

**Spoiler:** he lives. After Hansen's death, in Run This Town he maneuvers to put Chester Bennett in charge of Dogtown, or Jago Szabó ends up as colonel.

name: Cassius Ryder
appears: The Rescue · Chippin' In
note: Ripperdoc at Ryder's Clinic, on Pershing Street in Northside (Watson), the flagship of the Doc Ryder chain. On top of the standard stock, he does the **Smart-Link tattoos**: the Tyger Claws Dermal Imprint, free courtesy of Wakako Okada, and Johnny's tattoo in Chippin' In, "Johnny's Special" or "Together Forever", which is purely cosmetic. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, he sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes his stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. The wiki doesn't list his English voice.

name: Robert Rainwater
appears: Gig: Woman of La Mancha
note: Ripperdoc at Dr. Chrome, on a corner of Kabuki Market (Watson). He has the standard stock, although he himself is a ripper with no implants, opposed to cyberware in his own body. In the gig **Woman of La Mancha** there is a dialogue with him that asks for some Street Cred. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, he sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes his stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. Update 2.5 also adds a glamdoc in Kabuki, Issam Zahir, who restyles your arm cyberware; it is cosmetic only.

name: Charles Bucks
appears: Gig: Last Login
note:
Ripperdoc at an illegal basement clinic in northern Kabuki (Watson), supplied by the Scavengers. He has the standard stock, but the gig **Last Login** decides whether you keep him: take his bribe and he gives you a permanent **20% discount**; refuse it or attack him and you lose him as a vendor. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, he sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes his stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. English voice: Akie Kotabe.

**Spoiler:** his fate depends on what you decide in Last Login.

name: Nina Kraviz
appears: No guide jobs
note: Ripperdoc at Kraviz's Clinic, formerly her uncle's shop, in Charter Hill (Westbrook). She is a cameo by the Russian DJ Nina Kraviz, who plays herself (English voice included). She has the standard stock, nothing exclusive. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, she sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes her stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. Update 2.5 also adds a glamdoc in Charter Hill, Shō Gun Rose, who restyles your arm cyberware; it is cosmetic only.

name: Darius Clarke
appears: No guide jobs
note: Ripperdoc at a Doc Ryder clinic in Skyline West, Downtown (City Center). He has the standard stock and is the handiest ripperdoc in the city center, with no jobs of his own in the guide. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, he sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes his stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. Update 2.5 also adds a glamdoc in Downtown, Serena Zhao, who restyles your arm cyberware (Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire and Projectile Launch System); it is cosmetic only.

name: Santiago Molina
appears: No guide jobs
note: Ripperdoc at Molina's Clinic, in Wellsprings (Heywood); per the wiki's gallery, it is a Doc Ryder clinic. He has the standard stock and is close by if you do Padre's Heywood gigs or visit El Coyote Cojo. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, he sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes his stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. Each implant gets one random stat bonus at Tier 1 and another at Tier 2; the Chipware Connoisseur perk lets you reroll them.

name: Octavio Delgado
appears: No guide jobs
note: Ripperdoc at Octavio's Clinic, on the southeast edge of Rancho Coronado (Santo Domingo). He has the standard stock, nothing exclusive, and comes in handy if you do El Capitán's gigs in that area. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, he sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes his stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. Update 2.5 also adds a glamdoc in Rancho Coronado, Spite Vondell, who restyles your arm cyberware; it is cosmetic only.

name: Farida Nazeri
appears: Birds with Broken Wings · I've Seen That Face Before · Firestarter
note:
An Iranian-American ripperdoc, formerly with Militech, with her clinic in Golden Pacific, Dogtown (Phantom Liberty). Her story role is key: in Birds with Broken Wings she installs the **Behavioral Imprint-synced Faceplate**, the Iconic face implant you need to pass as one of the Cassel twins in Firestarter; that same job unlocks your second face slot. The wiki lists her as a cyberware vendor but doesn't confirm what stock she carries. The other Dogtown ripperdocs sell Phantom Liberty's 15 iconic implants. English voice: Shala Nyx.

**Spoiler:** she lives on every Phantom Liberty path.

name: Anthony Anderson
appears: Gig: Dogtown Saints
note: Ripperdoc at Haven Clinic, a church turned clinic on Montaña de Oro Ave, Golden Pacific, in Dogtown (Phantom Liberty). He is tied to the gig **Dogtown Saints**. Like the other Dogtown ripperdocs, he sells the standard stock plus Phantom Liberty's **15 iconic implants**, which you won't find anywhere else (except in Airdrops): Chrome Compressor, RAM Reallocator, COX-2, Axolotl, Kiroshi "Cockatrice", Rara Avis, Immovable Force, Adreno-trigger, Revulsor, Deep-field Visual Interface, Isometric Stabilizer, Electromag Recycler, Peripheral Inverse, Chitin and Leeroy Ligament System. His stock refreshes every 10 levels.

name: Hutch Spindler
appears: Aldecaldo camp
note: The ripperdoc at the Aldecaldos' mobile camp, in the Badlands. He has the standard stock and recommends stealth implants such as Optical Camo, although he doesn't sell clothing. He is the only fixed ripperdoc at hand while you do Panam's chain or Dakota Smith's gigs. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, he sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes his stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. The wiki doesn't list his English voice.

name: Sogo Watanabe
appears: No guide jobs
note: Ripperdoc at Instant Implants, in the Kabuki slums (Watson). The clinic has the standard stock, nothing exclusive, and is a nearby alternative to Viktor if you're already in Kabuki, where Robert Rainwater and Charles Bucks also work. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, it sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes its stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. Update 2.5 also adds a glamdoc in Kabuki, Issam Zahir, who restyles your arm cyberware; it is cosmetic only.

name: Chiyo Omoto
appears: No guide jobs
note: Ripperdoc at Medical Assistance, under the overpass next to Cherry Blossom Market, in Japantown (Westbrook). The clinic has the standard stock, nothing exclusive, and is useful if you lose Fingers as a vendor on Jig-Jig Street, since it's in the same district. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, it sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes its stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. Each implant gets one random stat bonus at Tier 1, another at Tier 2, and a third with the Driver Update perk.

name: Rafael Pérez
appears: No guide jobs
note: Ripperdoc at the Arroyo clinic, in Santo Domingo, a former Moore Technologies researcher. He has the standard stock, nothing exclusive, and is the nearest ripperdoc if you do El Capitán's gigs in Arroyo. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, he sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes his stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. From V's level 40, any ripperdoc also offers the Iconic Militech "Apogee" Sandevistan, for €$120,000.

name: Rony LaFleur
appears: No guide jobs
note: Ripperdoc at the West Wind Apartments, in West Wind Estate (Pacifica), the same building where Steve Sanchez lives. He serves "his own people" first, but takes V's eddies. He has the standard stock, nothing exclusive. Like every 2.x ripperdoc, he sells Tier 1 to 5 implants by V's level (Tier 2 shows up from level 10, Tier 3 from 20, Tier 4 from 30 and Tier 5 from 40), refreshes his stock every 10 levels and upgrades your implants for Item Components. Update 2.5 also adds a glamdoc in West Wind Estate, Zéna Delicé, who restyles your arm cyberware; it is cosmetic only.

name: Eron Acedo
appears: Dogtown (Phantom Liberty)
note: A ripperdoc working out of a bloodstained bathroom in the EBM Petrochem Stadium, in Dogtown (Phantom Liberty), near Herold Lowe. Like the other Dogtown ripperdocs, he sells the standard stock plus Phantom Liberty's **15 iconic implants**: Chrome Compressor, Kiroshi "Cockatrice", Rara Avis, Axolotl, COX-2, RAM Reallocator and the rest. Only these ripperdocs sell them; outside of them, you get them from repeating Airdrops, each guaranteeing one iconic until the pool runs out. Airdrops start in Lucretia My Reflection. His stock refreshes every 10 levels.

name: Costin Lahovary
appears: Dogtown (Phantom Liberty)
note: A former medtech who lost his license and now works at Lahovary's Clinic, in the Longshore Stacks market, Dogtown (Phantom Liberty). Like the other Dogtown ripperdocs, he sells the standard stock plus Phantom Liberty's **15 iconic implants**, among them the Chrome Compressor, the only Operating System that isn't a cyberdeck, Sandevistan or Berserk (up to +70 Cyberware Capacity at Tier 5). Outside Dogtown you only get them from Airdrops. His stock refreshes every 10 levels, and this is also where you upgrade your implants' Tier with Item Components.

name: Robert Wilson
appears: The Ripperdoc · The Rescue (side job The Gun)
note:
The owner of **2nd Amendment**, the gun shop in Megabuilding H10, opposite the elevator in V's building. From The Ripperdoc on, his side job **The Gun** is available: he gives you the Iconic **Dying Night** pistol, which gained a new iconic modifier in 2.0. A Streetkid V gets special "rite of passage" dialogue with him. If the job Shoot To Thrill is active, you can't get Dying Night until you finish it. Beyond that, he is a regular weapons vendor a few steps from your apartment.

**Spoiler:** he lives in every ending.

name: Herold Lowe
appears: Firestarter · Dogtown (Phantom Liberty)
note:
A black-market weapons vendor at the EBM Petrochem Stadium, in Dogtown (Phantom Liberty). He is the safety net for the **iconic weapons you missed** in the base game and the expansion: subject to his conditions, he sells the ones you didn't get, such as Errata (Disasterpiece), Satori (The Heist), Jinchu-Maru (Play It Safe), Widow Maker (Ghost Town), Butcher's Cleaver (M'ap Tann Pèlen), Doom Doom (Second Conflict) and Murphy's Law (Firestarter, Songbird path only). If a missable iconic slipped past you, check his stock before writing it off.

**Spoiler:** he lives.

name: Songbird
role: FIA netrunner; the heart of Phantom Liberty
appears: All of Phantom Liberty (Dog Eat Dog to Who Wants to Live Forever) · Nocturne Op55N1
note:
Song So Mi, a netrunner for the FIA (the NUSA's Federal Intelligence Agency), who contacts V to save President Myers when her plane is shot down over Dogtown in Dog Eat Dog; ignore her there and the expansion ends. In return she promises V a cure. Throughout Phantom Liberty she gives you points for the Relic perk tree and hunts for the cure in Hansen's hands. You never fight her as a boss: in Somewhat Damaged the Cerberus plays that role. In **Firestarter** you choose between helping her escape (Songbird path) or helping Reed capture her (Reed path); the choice is **permanent**. English voice: Minji Chang.

**Spoiler:** in King of Wands she flees to the Moon, is cured and leaves you a message (and the Quantum Tuner); in King of Swords you hand her over to Reed; in King of Cups you kill her at Cynosure because she asks you to; in King of Pentacles you spare her and she goes back to the NUSA as Myers' puppet. After Swords or Pentacles you can go on to The Tower.

name: Solomon Reed
role: FIA sleeper agent; Myers' man in Dogtown
appears: All of Phantom Liberty · Nocturne Op55N1 · Who Wants to Live Forever
note:
An FIA sleeper agent and former NUSA special forces operative, President Myers' trusted man in Night City. You reach him from Capitán Caliente at the end of Lucretia My Reflection, and from then on he is your partner in Dogtown; while living undercover he worked as a bouncer for Dino Dinovic. In Firestarter you can help him capture Songbird, and his path continues with Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos, Cynosure and the Cerberus. He can't be taken down non-lethally. Calling him from the Nocturne Op55N1 rooftop (or in Who Wants to Live Forever) starts The Tower ending. The wiki doesn't list his English voice.

**Spoiler:** in King of Wands you kill him at the NCX spaceport (he drops his **Pariah** pistol). In King of Swords and King of Pentacles he lives and offers you the cure; in King of Cups he lives as a drifter and calls you from Dayton. If you refuse the cure, he berates you.

name: Alex
role: FIA agent; runs The Moth bar
appears: The Damned · Get It Together · You Know My Name · Birds with Broken Wings · I've Seen That Face Before · Firestarter · Unfinished Sympathy
note:
Alena "Alex" Xenakis, an FIA agent and Reed's old colleague, who runs The Moth bar in Dogtown. You meet her in The Damned, when she and Reed follow Songbird's trail to Slider. In Birds with Broken Wings you can spend a night with her at The Moth (it isn't a romance) and take the **Osprey** rifle from her armory. In I've Seen That Face Before she poses as whichever Cassel twin you aren't playing, and she goes with you to the interview with Hansen in Firestarter. English voice: Yvonne Senat Jones.

**Spoiler:** on the Songbird path she kills Hansen and lives; in King of Wands you meet her in Unfinished Sympathy and she leaves you a Monte Carlo postcard. On the Reed path (Cups or Pentacles), Hansen executes her in Firestarter.

name: Kurt Hansen
appears: Dog Eat Dog · Spider and the Fly · You Know My Name · Birds with Broken Wings · Firestarter
note:
The BARGHEST colonel who rules Dogtown, formerly with Militech, and Phantom Liberty's antagonist. He owns the Black Sapphire, the hotel-casino where he throws the You Know My Name party, and according to Songbird he holds the cure she is after. In Firestarter he interviews you while you pose as one of the Cassel twins: have the You Know My Name roulette result at hand, because he asks. On the Reed path he is the **boss** at the market exit; sources disagree on whether he switches to melee at 75% (game8) or 50% health (wiki). He drops the Iconic **Fang** pistol. English voice: Eliah Mountjoy.

**Spoiler:** he always dies in Firestarter: on the Songbird path Alex kills him with no fight; on the Reed path, you face him yourself.

name: Rosalind Myers
appears: Dog Eat Dog · Hole in the Sky · Spider and the Fly · Lucretia My Reflection · Somewhat Damaged · Leave in Silence
note:
President of the New United States and former Militech CEO. Her plane, Space Force One, goes down in Dogtown at the start of Phantom Liberty and Songbird asks you to save her. You escort her across Dogtown to the Kress Street hideout in Lucretia My Reflection, where you decide what to do with two strangers (Taylor Gibbs and Jacob Long) and put her in touch with Solomon Reed. When she leaves, she leaves her Iconic assault rifle **Hawk** behind: pick it up, because it is missable. English voice: Kay Bess.

**Spoiler:** she survives if you rescue her. In Leave in Silence she thanks you with the NUSA distinction (+€$30,000) if you spared So Mi, or a token €$5,000 if you killed her. In The Devil she denounces Saburo's return.

name: Aurore Cassel
appears: You Know My Name · Birds with Broken Wings · I've Seen That Face Before · Firestarter
note:
A EuroBank netrunner and former member of The Collective, Aymeric's twin. They are Hansen's guests, and Songbird plans to work with them on the cure he holds. In You Know My Name you scan her behavior by playing roulette at her table, and in I've Seen That Face Before you intercept them from the trunk of their car: listen to the whole conversation about Slider's death. A feminine V poses as Aurore in Firestarter. In Hansen's interview, say you don't know any "Raquel" (she was in the prison's VIP wing), that your fashion contact is Kerry Eurodyne's tailor, and don't take the drink (or give it to her). English voice: Leonie Schliesing.

**Spoiler:** Alex and Reed kill her. If you heard the conversation, you download "Blind_n_Dead" from her body, which unlocks the side job Voodoo Treasure.

name: Aymeric Cassel
appears: You Know My Name · Birds with Broken Wings · I've Seen That Face Before · Firestarter
note:
A netrunner and Aurore's twin, a former member of The Collective and an ex-Petrochem employee. Both are Hansen's guests at the Black Sapphire party in You Know My Name, and Songbird plans to work with them on the cure; there you scan his behavior by playing roulette, and it pays to note whether the twins win or lose the final bet, because Hansen asks about it in Firestarter. In I've Seen That Face Before you take over their car from the trunk and drive them into Reed and Alex's trap. A masculine V poses as Aymeric in Firestarter; Alex plays Aurore. English voice: André Refig.

**Spoiler:** Alex and Reed kill him in the I've Seen That Face Before trap.

name: Jago Szabó
appears: Birds with Broken Wings · Run This Town
note:
BARGHEST's chief accountant and one of the candidates to inherit Dogtown when Hansen dies. His photo is on the board of BARGHEST's top brass you see in the basement in Birds with Broken Wings. His real weight comes in **Run This Town**, the job Mr. Hands offers you after Firestarter: while it is pending, no new Dogtown gigs open, and if you refuse it twice it fails (Mr. Hands doubles the pay once first). There you decide whom to back in the succession between Szabó and Chester Bennett, Mr. Hands' candidate.

**Spoiler:** Bennett's men kill him at Hansen's funeral, unless you back him and deal with Bennett (then he becomes colonel) or force peace.

name: Slider
appears: The Damned · Get It Together · I've Seen That Face Before
note:
Wilky "Slider" LaGuerre, a Voodoo Boys netrunner hiding at Dogtown's Eventide Resort & Spa. In The Damned, Reed and Alex follow Songbird's trail through him: you can get into his hideout by talking to the guards (easier if you spared Placide and Brigitte) or through the vents (code **230598**), and you jack into his device. The gig Treating Symptoms gives you the key to the locked room in his hideout, with the **Gris-Gris** revolver. In I've Seen That Face Before, the Cassel twins talk about his death and a stash: listen to the whole conversation to unlock Voodoo Treasure (code **941229**, under The Needle, with the **Rook** pistol and €$8000).

**Spoiler:** he is already dead when you arrive.

name: Taylor Gibbs
role: Squatter at the Kress Street hideout
appears: Lucretia My Reflection
note:
One of the two people already living in the Rindo Hotel hideout, on Elizabeth Kress Street, when you bring President Myers there in Lucretia My Reflection; the other is Jacob Long. **Save before talking to them.** You can neutralize them (a fight, you pick up one of the bodies and there's a time skip; the next morning Johnny points out the first airdrop) or make a deal so they stay (Jacob points out the airdrop).
